content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Trusting reliance on God—especially confidence in Jesus Christ and his saving work—expressed through commitment, obedience, and hope rather than mere intellectual agreement.","primary_basis":["Hebrews 11:1, 6—faith is assurance regarding what is hoped for and conviction regarding what is unseen, grounded in approaching God.","Ephesians 2:8–9—salvation is received by grace through faith, not earned by works.","Romans 3:21–28; 5:1—justification and peace with God are associated with faith in Jesus Christ.","Galatians 2:16, 20—life and justification are described in relation to faith in Christ.","John 3:16; 20:30–31—believing in Christ is linked with eternal life.","Mark 11:22–24—faith denotes trust in God, particularly in prayer.","James 2:14–26—living faith is shown by corresponding action rather than remaining mere verbal assent."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Faithfulness, fidelity, or loyal allegiance to God or Christ. This reading emphasizes enduring covenant loyalty and obedient commitment, and is sometimes debated in passages traditionally translated as “faith in Christ.”","basis":["Habakkuk 2:4; Romans 1:17—the righteous live by faith or faithfulness.","Galatians 5:22—the same Greek word group can denote faithfulness.","Romans 3:22; Galatians 2:16—the phrase pistis Christou is variously interpreted as faith in Christ, Christ’s faithfulness, or participation in Christ’s fidelity.","Revelation 2:10, 13; 14:12—faith is closely associated with steadfast loyalty under pressure."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"“The faith” as the received body of Christian belief, apostolic teaching, or communal confession rather than an individual act of trust.","basis":["Jude 3—“the faith” was once for all entrusted to the saints.","Acts 6:7—people become obedient to “the faith.”","1 Timothy 4:1, 6; 2 Timothy 4:7—faith can denote the Christian message or confession preserved and followed."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Faith as a special Spirit-given capacity for unusual confidence in God, distinguished from the faith ordinarily expected of Christians.","basis":["1 Corinthians 12:9—faith is listed among particular gifts of the Spirit.","1 Corinthians 13:2—exceptional faith capable of “moving mountains” is distinguished rhetorically.","Matthew 17:20—mustard-seed faith is associated with extraordinary efficacy."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Faith primarily as intellectual assent to revealed propositions or acceptance of doctrine.","basis":["Romans 10:9–10—belief includes confessing truths about Jesus and his resurrection.","1 Corinthians 15:1–5—the gospel received in faith contains definite claims about Christ’s death and resurrection.","James 2:19—doctrinal belief alone is acknowledged but judged insufficient, making this a component rather than the usual complete definition."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad consensus that faith centrally involves trustful reliance on God or Christ, but no single settled symbolic definition covers every biblical use. “Faith” is ordinarily treated as a theological disposition or relationship rather than as a symbol in the strict sense. Its semantic range also includes faithfulness, allegiance, a body of doctrine, and a particular spiritual gift."}
